title: HEAD_DIM 64 + 2^18 batch at device batch 128 (2x2 corner)
description: Three hyperparameter lines: HEAD_DIM 128->64 (8 heads instead of 4, identical params/FLOPs/VRAM), TOTAL_BATCH_SIZE 2**17->2**18, DEVICE_BATCH_SIZE 64->128 (grad_accum stays 1).
reflection: val_bpb 0.994496; 1770 steps, 464.0M tokens, MFU 37.15%, peak VRAM 45.0GB. The throughput claim held: device batch 128 processed 464M tokens on a HOT card, matching the 462M that round 0's cold-card run needed an idle GPU to reach, and +11% over the hot-card 2^17 replicas (~418M). So ~46M tokens were bought back purely by kernel efficiency, at the cost of halving optimizer steps (3200 -> 1770), which round 0 showed is a flat axis. Score is 0.0020 below the five-fold replicated hot-card median (0.99646) and 0.0018 ABOVE the lucky cold-card number that is currently called the baseline. Honest caveat: 0.0020 is almost exactly 1 sd of the replication noise measured in round 0, so this single run does not establish the effect on its own - it needs to be read against a0's HEAD_DIM-only and a1's batch-only runs as the fourth cell of the 2x2. VRAM doubled 22.2 -> 45.0GB, which is where the original baseline lived, so there is no headroom problem but also little headroom left for growing the model at device batch 128.
